title: implement 2D minimal convolutions

atoms.evidence: oh = h - kh + 1; ow = w - kw + 1 (minimal form, no stride/padding)
s_b, s_ic, s_h, s_w = x.stride() — pulls all 4 input strides
x_strided = x.as_strided(size=(b, ic, oh, ow, kh, kw), stride=(s_b, s_ic, s_h, s_w, s_h, s_w)) — 2-spatial-dim windowing; output_h/output_w windows reuse the same h/w strides as the kernel dims
einops.einsum(x_strided, weights, 'b ic oh ow kh kw, oc ic kh kw -> b oc oh ow')
the exercise IS this atom — 6D strided view + einsum for 2D conv from scratch
ic on both sides of einsum spec — contracted dimension
weights: Float[Tensor, 'out_channels in_channels kernel_height kernel_width'] — the proposed 4D conv-kernel-shape atom in its canonical form

notes: 7-atom exercise — exact 2D mirror of 0_2_18. The duplication of strides (stride=(s_b, s_ic, s_h, s_w, s_h, s_w)) is the subtle teaching point — the OUTPUT spatial dims share strides with the KERNEL spatial dims, because both index into the same input rows/columns. Re-confirms conv-windowing-2d, conv-channel-sum, conv-kernel-shape.
